h1: Life in the UK mock test
intro: Try our free Life in the UK mock test and find out if you’re ready for the real thing. Answer 24 questions against the clock, get your score straight away, and see an explanation for every question you get wrong.

sections.heading: About this Life in the UK mock test
sections.text:
Like the real test, our Life in the UK mock test gives you 24 questions and 45 minutes, and you need 18 right to pass. Questions are drawn at random from our question bank, so each mock test is different.

Prefer to learn as you go? Turn on learning mode and the answer appears after every question.

sections.heading: Who needs the Life in the UK test?
sections.text:
Most people aged 18 to 64 must pass the test before applying for:
- [Indefinite Leave to Remain](/indefinite-leave-to-remain-ilr/), also called settlement
- [British citizenship](/british-citizenship/) by naturalisation

You only pass once. The same reference number works for both applications, even years apart.

sections.heading: Example questions
sections.text:
A few questions of the kind you’ll find in our Life in the UK mock test:
- Which countries make up Great Britain? England, Scotland and Wales.
- Who defeated Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815? The Duke of Wellington.
- How many people sit on a jury in England and Wales? 12.
- What is Hogmanay? New Year’s Eve in Scotland.

Start the mock test above to try a full set of 24 questions, marked instantly.

sections.heading: Topics in the test
sections.text:
Questions come from the official handbook, Life in the United Kingdom: A Guide for New Residents. Expect questions on British values, history, traditions, sport and culture, famous people, and how government and the law work.

Our mock test questions are our own, written to cover the same ground. The Home Office doesn’t publish the real questions.

sections.heading: How to prepare
sections.text:
Read the handbook properly, then use mock tests to find your weak spots. Most people who fail haven’t read the whole book, or rush the questions on the day. Aim to score at least 20 out of 24 in our Life in the UK mock test several times in a row before you book.

It also helps to study in short sessions over two or three weeks rather than the night before. Make a list of dates, names and numbers you keep forgetting, and test yourself on them each day.

sections.heading: Booking and on the day
sections.text: Book online at least 3 days ahead. The test costs £50. Take the same photo ID you booked with, or you won’t be allowed in. Results are given on the day, and if you pass you get a reference number for your application.

sections.heading: Ready to apply?
sections.text: Once you’ve passed, the next step is usually your settlement or citizenship application. Our Manchester team checks your time outside the UK, your English evidence and your documents before anything is sent. Check when you can apply with our [ILR eligibility checker](/am-i-eligible-for-ilr/).

faqs.q: Is the Life in the UK mock test free?
faqs.a: Yes, completely free, with no sign-up. Take it as many times as you like.

faqs.q: Does a Life in the UK test pass expire?
faqs.a: No. Once you’ve passed, the pass stays valid for ILR and citizenship applications.
You can book again after 7 days. You pay the £50 fee each time.

faqs.q: Are these the real Life in the UK questions?
faqs.a: No. The Home Office doesn’t publish the real questions. Ours are written to cover the topics in the official handbook.

faqs.q: Can I take the test in another language?
faqs.a: The test is in English. If you live in Wales or Scotland, you can choose to take it in Welsh or Scottish Gaelic instead.
